summary:
Oh my Earth! is a bilingual (Thai–English) interactive website that transforms complex NASA Earth observation data into accessible visualizations and engaging learning experiences.

Our platform addresses the challenge of making scientific data easier to access, interpret, and understand, especially for students and the general public. Through our Guess the Graph game, users predict environmental trends, compare their answers with real observations, and discover relationships between natural variables. Interactive tools, including a Global Hotspot Map, World Explorer, and Thailand Explorer, allow users to investigate environmental changes across different locations and time periods, identify long-term trends, and explore their statistical significance.

In today's data-rich world, we believe information is only valuable when people can understand and learn from it. Earth is our shared home, and everyone deserves to know how it is changing. By combining scientific exploration with gamification, we aim to spark curiosity, strengthen critical thinking, and make Earth science enjoyable and meaningful for everyone.

Our mission is not just to help people understand data, but to help them understand the planet we call home.
details:
🚀 1. Project Overview

Oh my EARTH!, developed by Team Far Side of the Moon, is a bilingual (Thai–English) interactive educational platform that makes NASA Earth observation data more accessible, engaging, and understandable to everyone.

Our platform combines gamification, interactive visualizations, and scientific analysis to help users explore environmental changes, discover relationships between natural variables, and develop data literacy.

🎮 2. How It Works

Our platform offers four main features:

🎯 Guess the Graph — Learn Through Play

Players become Earth Trend Detectives by predicting environmental changes through two game modes:

  • Trend Prediction: Draw the continuation of a partially hidden environmental time series.
  • Relationship Prediction: Observe one environmental variable and predict how another variable changes.

For example, players can explore the relationship between rainfall and PM2.5, predicting how changes in rainfall might relate to air pollution levels.

After submitting their predictions, players compare their drawings with actual observations, receive accuracy scores, and discover the scientific explanations behind the patterns.

🗺️ Global Hotspot Map — Discover Environmental Changes

An interactive world map highlights regions where temperature, rainfall, humidity, and sunlight show notable changes between 2001 and 2024.

🌐 World Explorer — Explore Global Environmental Data

Users can investigate environmental records at 195 capital-city coordinates, allowing them to examine environmental trends across different geographical regions.

🇹🇭 Thailand Explorer — Connect Science to Local Communities

Users can compare Thai provinces across 12 environmental measurements, including haze, soil moisture, and runoff, making Earth science relevant to their local surroundings.

📊 3. Scientific Analysis

Users can explore monthly observations, annual averages, and seasonally adjusted data to distinguish seasonal fluctuations from long-term environmental changes.

The platform also displays rates of change and statistical confidence, helping users understand whether observed trends are supported by sufficient evidence.

💡 4. Creativity and Innovation

Rather than passively reading scientific graphs, users actively predict, investigate, and verify environmental patterns using real observations.

Our innovation lies in combining game-based learning, scientific data exploration, and statistical interpretation in a single bilingual platform that makes complex environmental information approachable for non-experts.

🌱 5. Benefits and Intended Impact

Earth is our shared home, and everyone deserves to understand how it is changing.

By transforming complex Earth science data into engaging learning experiences, we aim to inspire curiosity, strengthen critical thinking, and increase environmental awareness among children, students, and the general public.

Our goal is to make scientific knowledge accessible beyond research communities and encourage people to investigate the environmental changes happening around them.

We want people not just to understand data, but to understand the planet they call home.

🛠️ 6. Tools, Technologies, and Data Sources

Software: TypeScript, React 18, Vite 5, d3-geo (globe and maps), Vercel serverless functions, Upstash Redis (game questions), Vitest, GitHub Actions. Python and a local PostgreSQL database prepare the World explorer caches.

NASA data

  • NASA POWER monthly point API (MERRA-2, CERES): air temperature, daily high and low, rainfall, humidity, wind speed, sunlight
  • NASA Giovanni: GPM IMERG V07 (satellite rainfall), GLDAS Noah 2.1 (soil moisture, runoff, evapotranspiration), MERRA-2 M2T1NXAER (aerosol optical depth), OCO-2 GEOS Level 3 (column CO₂, 2015 to 2021), AIRS AIRX3C2M (one game question)
  • NASA Blue Marble imagery (home page)

Other data: GISTDA Sphere flood recurrence API, geoBoundaries (Thailand provinces), Natural Earth (country outlines and land mask), REST Countries (capital coordinates), Hawaii Ocean Time-series (one game question).

Methods: Thailand explorer: seasonal cycle removed, Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope. World explorer and Hotspot map: seasonal Kendall and Sen slope with a year-block bootstrap (999 resamples) for a 95% range and p-value. CO₂: descriptive slope only.

AI: Claude (Anthropic) helped write code, designs and documentation, reviewed and tested by the team.
